newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Midcontinent traders retreat to the sidelines.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Midcontinent traders retreat to the sidelines.

text.p: Many U.S. Midcontinent refined products traders retreated to the sidelines on Monday as a rally in heating oil and unleaded futures sent cash prices sharply higher, traders said.
"The market is just kind of frozen," one Midwest trader said of spot activity in the Group Three and Chicago markets.

NYMEX January heating oil finish up 3.11 cents a gallon at 74.82 cents after hitting a contract high 75.70 cents. Front-month gasoline made a similar upward move, ending up 2.48 cents a gallon at 69.52 cents on the day on forecasts of a prolonged cold spell sweeping the country.

The dramatic shifts in futures prices over the past week, capped by the surging prices today, startled Midwest traders expecting spot prices to generally weaken through the month on plentiful stocks in the region.
"The moves have been so severe, you could have either made a fortune or lost a fortune in this market," a Group Three trader said.

With few deals heard done, differentials were called largely unchanged in the Group Three and Chicago markets. But traders said differentials should ease against the firmer futures prices once the NYMEX rally tops out.
Prompt unleaded gasoline was bid 4.25 cents a gallon in Group Three and one cent weaker in Chicago, traders said.
